definition_audit.object: letI MeasurableSpace(Matrix d d ℝ) := borel _
definition_audit.audit: Fixes the ordinary Borel measurable structure on actual precision matrices. It is a local structure assignment, not a hypothesis or user-supplied sigma algebra.

The supplied body is Measure.haarMeasure on the whole compact O(n), normalized on top PositiveCompacts. Thus it denotes the full normalized Haar law, agreeing with S2. Its separate compiled specification was not read or re-approved here. Haar existence/normalization remains a producer fact, not a new binder.

Exactly 2 times the restriction of full Haar to det=+1 and det=-1. Source S2 gives each event mass 1/2, so these are the two source conditional probability laws. Event measurability and half-mass are internal facts. No independently supplied prior or arbitrary weighting appears.
Supplied body is ((κ+1)/2)I-((κ-1)/4)(O+Oᵀ), exactly Eq4 for every source orthogonal O. Matrix identity and scalar multiplication match the source real matrix operations.

The supplied coordinate equivalence first swaps intra-block and block indices, then uses standard finite-product indexing, followed by residual concatenation. Thus contiguous size-n blocks carry A_Oj, off-diagonal blocks are zero, and the residual is I_(d%n). Euclidean division gives k=d/n=floor(d/n), r=d%n=d-kn on the source range. At r=0 the residual index is empty and no r>0 hypothesis appears. Volume preservation is a later internal bridge, not granted merely by the finite equivalence.

Measure.pi over Fin(d/n) forms independent copies of the corresponding fixed-sign conditional law. Mapping that product by blockPrecision is exactly the source D_b as the law of the random block precision. No product target law is substituted for this prior construction.

The supplied multivariateGaussian body is the image of a standard Gaussian by the covariance square-root map with zero mean. For source-supported SPD A this is N(0,A⁻¹), with A⁻¹ as covariance, not precision. The total library function is defined on all matrices, but only D_b-a.e. admissible matrices affect its bind. SPD support and Gaussian kernel measurability must be discharged internally. This is not a source claim about off-support indefinite matrices.

definition_audit.object: Mpos := Dpos.bind γ; Mneg := Dneg.bind γ
definition_audit.audit: These are actual averages of inverse-precision Gaussian laws under the source random matrix priors, exactly the left meaning of Eq6. They are not defined as P_b tensor powers or as functions of the desired affinity.

sqrt(det A_O)/(2π)^(real n/2) times exp(-xᵀA_Ox/2) is the correct Lebesgue density of N(0,A_O⁻¹) on the source SPD domain. The real exponent (n:ℝ)/2 retains odd dimensions. The standard Gaussian-density identification is source-implied background, rather than a separately printed author proof at Ex71.

The formulas average the actual p O x against the actual conditional priors. This is a valid representative of the source mixture density p_b once inner integrability and the mixture withDensity identity are derived internally. Real Bochner integration totalizes to zero if not integrable; the proof must exclude that artifact for every source x. Source positivity/spectral bounds and finite prior mass suffice; no L1 gate is a binder.

Exactly the Lebesgue integral of sqrt(qpos*qneg) on EuclideanSpace n. The unqualified integral uses its canonical Euclidean volume. With the actual block-density bridge this is source Ex68 for actual P_±. It is not a free parameter, an estimate, or a desired ambient kth root.

The supplied rnDeriv body chooses the measurable density of the Lebesgue decomposition when it exists, otherwise zero. It is not pointwise a specified Gaussian-mixture density. On the actual probability laws, finite-dimensional volume is sigma-finite, the canonical withDensity producer gives AC, and RN uniqueness identifies the derivative a.e. with the finite nonnegative real density in ofReal form. These facts exclude both the rnDeriv no-decomposition fallback and toReal(∞)=0 from the source observable a.e. No pointwise equality of arbitrary density versions is claimed.

sqrt((dMpos/dvolume).toReal * (dMneg/dvolume).toReal) uses the actual ambient measures. Once the internal RN-density identification is established it equals the source ambient square-root density product a.e. Its integral is density-representative independent, on canonical Euclidean volume.
These strengthen the conclusion by exposing the ordinary density meaning and finite integral already implicit in the source. Their conjunction does not weaken the equality or add source assumptions.
